properties.name: The changelog shows a balance, counted from the status snapshot each release now keeps at its cut
properties.rationale: Built to the accepted dec:how-the-changelog-balance-is-counted (option C) for req:a-changelog-shows-what-was-taken-away-beside-what-was-added: a status move is not a change on the time axis, so only a snapshot each release keeps can count what was taken away without reading "0 dropped" where 11 were. Additive only, because Alex and others use the MCP surface as it is: each reply gained one field and nothing else moved. A snapshot is never rewritten, and none is taken for a release whose cut is past, because what a release saw must not move and today's statuses are not what it saw. Back-filling past releases from the design copy committed at each tag is in the decision and is NOT built here: a named follow-up. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: release_includes_all with apply now keeps the release's status snapshot (every Requirement, Capability, Decision and Verification status, with discontinued), stored on a Snapshot linked to the release, whole the first time and as a delta from the previous release's after that; its reply gains `status_snapshot`. changelog_view's draft gains `balance`: requirements added against dropped or deferred, capabilities added against removed or withdrawn, decisions accepted against reversed, checks gone from passing to failing, and the window's test_failure_fix changes, each with how it was counted; an end with no snapshot is named and never zero. New module crates/reflow2-core/src/balance.rs; snapshots_of and prior_state_coverage skip status snapshots; both tool descriptions and toolsnaps updated; two edge readers listed in schema/derived/edge_readers.yaml.
